doc.title: Jim Cullum interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007

title: Transcribed solos and the difficulty of playing improvised solos
summary: Cullum is amazed at seeing his solos written out; Teagarden could not play his own transcribed solos.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Um hum. Have you ever had an opportunity where someone writes out one of your solos, transcribes one of your solos?
Yes? And then you’ve looked at it?
Yeah. And I am amazed you know, I see it. Yeah, this happens. Jack Teagarden said that guys had written out some of his solos and he couldn’t play them, he couldn’t play them.

Well an improvised solo is a very hard to thing to play. I’ve played some Armstrong solos. To play somebody else’s improvised solo is — because play a piece of music, play it in a big band, they may have some complicated rhythms and things like that in it, but they’re usually not as complicated and difficult as an improvised solo.
Everybody’s solo may have some twists and turns in it that are just almost impossible for you to —
